newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close up at new highs, pork bellies weak.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close up at new highs, pork bellies weak.

text.p: CME hogs closed strong with October setting a new contract high after December set a new high earlier. Pork bellies ended weak after profit taking and long liquidation, traders said.
October hogs set a new contract high of 57.350 cents in the closing range and December set a new high earlier at 57.500. Hogs closed up 1.175 to off 0.050 with October up most at 57.300 cents.
Demand reflected expectations that cash hog markets will show continued strength next week as active pork product markets encourage strong packer interest, they said.
"Packers want to fill the (pork) pipeline -- it seems pretty empty right now," said Scott Shepard with Cargill Investor Services.
Some short covering was also evident ahead of the monthly Cold Storage report. That report is expected to show generally tight frozen ham and belly stocks, traders added.
Cargill Investor Services, Lind-Waldock, Rand Financials, Dean Witter and Prudential Securities were all cited as early buyers in October, pit sources said.

Pork bellies ran up along with hogs, but turned down midday when local selling and mixed profit taking developed near technical resistance. February again met technical resistance near the 80.000 cent area and this sent prices tumbling for net losses on sell stops, traders said.

Demand from a rising cash market had boosted prices early. Belly prices jumped $10 per cwt this week and expectations are for cash to rise another $10 next week to the mid $80's. However, some traders voiced concern that the sharp rise in cash prices may again turn off retail demand. There was also positioning ahead of Friday afternoon's Cold Storage report.
The report may end up to be bullish on light stocks, but February is still a long way off and futures usually trade technically until later in the fall, they added.
Estimates on September 1 U.S. frozen pork belly stocks ranged from 18.1 to 25.2 million lbs, compared with 28.5 million last month and 17.4 million a year ago.
Merrill Lynch and R.J. O'Brien were on both sides of the market. Lind-Waldock and Prudential Securities bought early.
Pork bellies closed 0.250 to 0.900 lower with February off 0.375 cents at 78.375 cents.
